page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc8a.48xlarge is an ECS Bare Metal server instance built for high-density compute tasks. Driven by dedicated AMD EPYC 9T24 processors clocked at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the machine delivers a total of 192 dedicated vCPUs. Hypervisor overhead is eliminated via bare-metal provisioning supported by KVM infrastructure. System memory is provisioned at 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding a lean 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

Network connectivity features a high-throughput baseline bandwidth of 64 Gbps, facilitating rapid node-to-node communication in distributed topologies. The instance contains zero local disk storage and lacks integrated hardware accelerators or GPUs. Storage dependencies rely entirely on attached cloud disks over the network, making storage architecture an important design consideration for data-intensive pipelines.

Cost efficiency is focused around massive compute density rather than integrated storage or memory expansion. The allocation of 192 dedicated physical threads under a 2.0 GB per core balance avoids unnecessary RAM expenses for compute-heavy applications. Primary workload fits include high-performance computing (HPC), parallel batch processing, large-scale continuous integration and compilation jobs, and distributed microservices architectures that do not require extensive per-core memory.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc8a.48xlarge is a dedicated ECS Bare Metal compute-optimized server powered by AMD EPYC 9T24 processors running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Designed for compute-heavy parallel workloads, it provides 192 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a focused 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server operates with KVM bare-metal virtualization, eliminating hypervisor overhead for latency-critical processing. Networking capability is substantial, featuring a 64 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance features no local storage and zero GPUs, requiring remote network block storage for persistent data. This hardware profile provides high compute density without incurring the cost of surplus RAM, making it well matched for parallel scientific computing, batch processing pipelines, high-density container clusters, and distributed video encoding.
